2024_190_m022724bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held February 27, 2024 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order at 7:01 p.m. by President Schmidt and adjourned at 9:08 p.m. before an audience of approximately 200. The Board approved a nine-item consent agenda and four bond-related business items, among them elementary playground site work totaling $3,116,644.10 and a $161,200.00 professional moving services award to Premier Relocations, LLC. Ten members of the public spoke, most of them Troy Education Association members addressing the expired teachers' contract, after which President Schmidt read a bargaining statement citing tentative agreement on 18 contractual items.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, February 27, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Called to order by President Schmidt at 7:01 p.m.; adjourned at 9:08 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh); document filed with the March 19, 2024 meeting packet.

**Attendance**
President Schmidt, plus Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Fulcher, and West. Approximately 200 members of the audience.

**Student Representative Reports**
Schmidt moved student reports first on the agenda so students could attend the Athens vs. Troy High varsity basketball game. Marlien William (Athens High) reported Charity Week raised $166,439.53 for Love for a Child; The Giving Foundation matched 100% of the total, for a grand total of $332,879.06. Jayla Turner (Troy High) reported Activist Week raised $38,822 for the Troy-based nonprofit On My Own. Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East) and Teagan Pruitt (Troy College and Career High School) also reported.

**Recognition**
- All-State Athletes, Fall 2023, presented by Director of Athletics Tim Fulcher: Derek Blackwell, Marc Delikat, Adam Ethridge, Rintaro Goda, Jack Hotts, Prabhath Inturi, Derrick Kim, Eric Kim, Alex Marine, Neel Nagappala, Rohan Nagaram, Nish Palepu, Vishvaa Ravishankar (Cross Country), Josh Samuelson, Adriano Shauya, and Ava Weeks (Girls' Golf).
- Athens Boys' Soccer, MHSAA Division 1 State Champions, won November 4th at Grand Ledge High School; season record of 20 wins, 3 losses, and 2 ties, ending on a 17-game winning streak. The 7th boys' soccer state title in school history; Athens has 17 MHSAA state titles.
- Coach of the Year Andrew Shipp (Boys' Tennis), Michigan High School Tennis Coaches Association; 18th year leading Athens Varsity Tennis plus 5 years of JV; second award, first in 2011; 8th place finish at the State Finals in Midland.
- Coach of the Year Todd Heugh (Boys' Soccer), Michigan High School Soccer Coaches Association; 13th season with Athens; third award, first in 2002 at Rochester High School and second in 2019 at Athens; also named Great Lakes Regional Coach of the Year by the United Soccer Coaches Association.
- Superintendent Student Advisory Board Executive Committee, which leads the 54-member SSAB and organized the MLK Citywide Celebration and Day of Service: Marlien William, Aanya Shah, Nurayda Albeez, Kara Crepeau, Elyse Lazrado, Maaz Ali, Niveditha Chandrakanth, and Rachel Asirvatham.
- Student Spotlight: Jack Kelly, Athens High School senior, for drone technology; Thomas Butcher presented, with a video shown to the Board.
- Board Recognition Month, postponed from the January 16 meeting because school closed January 16th for inclement weather.

**Consent Agenda**
Moved by Hauff, supported by Haupt; items A through I approved. Yes: 7, No: 0. Items: January 9, 2024 Workshop minutes; January 16, 2024 Organizational & Regular Meeting minutes; Treasurer's Report - December 2023; Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; Schools of Choice 105 & 105c; Course Description Book & New Graduation Requirements; Updated Section 1 Resolution; Districtwide Lawn Mowing 2024-2026; and cancellation of the March 9, 2024 Board Winter Retreat.

**Business** (Deputy Superintendent Rick West noted all items were discussed at the February 6th Board Workshop and all relate to Bond work)

| Item | Vendor | Amount |
|---|---|---|
| Summer 2024 professional moving services | Premier Relocations, LLC | $161,200.00 |
| Playground concrete | Albanelli Cement Contractors | $394,700.00 |
| Playground earthwork (Barnard, Bemis, Morse) | Dalco Services, LLC | $633,828.00 |
| Playground earthwork (Hill, Martell, Troy Union) | Jacklyn Contracting | $697,000.00 |
| Playground landscape | Dalco Services, LLC | $344,153.00 |
| Playground asphalt paving | Nagle Paving Company | $763,650.00 |
| Playground bid total | | $2,833,331.00 |
| Playground contingency | | $283,333.10 |
| Playground TOTAL | | $3,116,644.10 |
| Troy HS athletics temporary fencing | Fencing Connection | $92,540.00 |

The Athens HS Stadium Turf and Baker MS Track replacement award was also approved, charged to the 2023 Capital Projects Fund and the Building Site and Sinking Fund; the minutes carry no dollar figures for it. All four business votes were Yes: 7, No: 0.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda)**
Janice Boyer, Peggy Chinoski, Alex Karpowitsch (declined to speak, supplied SAT score data), Gary Koskinen, Katie Starn, Mike DeSantis, Jacob Ritter, Brian Fahnestock, Jamie Hallmark, and TEA President Jason Cichowicz. Most addressed the expired Collective Bargaining Agreement.

**Other**
The Board cast its MASB Board of Directors ballot for Birgit McQuiston, Region 8, three-year term (moved Philippart, supported Wilson; Yes: 7, No: 0). Schmidt reported tentative agreement with the TEA on 18 specific contractual items, a full bargaining day on February 22nd, and future bargaining dates of March 13, March 19, April 3, April 10, and April 16.

Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, held February 27, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson were present, along with Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Fulcher, and West. Approximately 200 members of the audience attended. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation GH/jh. The document is carried under the March 19, 2024 meeting date.

STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE REPORTS. President Schmidt moved the student reports to first on the agenda so that students could leave to attend the Athens vs. Troy High varsity basketball game. Marlien William, student representative for Athens High School, reported on events and activities at Athens and announced that the total raised during Charity Week for Love for a Child was $166,439.53. The Giving Foundation matched 100% of the total raised, resulting in a grand total of $332,879.06. Jayla Turner, student representative for Troy High School, reported on events and activities at her school and shared that Activist Week raised $38,822 for On My Own, a Troy-based nonprofit. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, and Teagan Pruitt, student representative for Troy College and Career High School (TCCHS), each reported on events and activities in their schools.

RECOGNITION - ALL-STATE ATHLETES FALL 2023. Mr. Tim Fulcher, Director of Athletics, recognized students named All-State Athletes in their respective sports: Derek Blackwell (Boys' Tennis), Marc Delikat (Boys' Soccer), Adam Ethridge (Boys' Soccer), Rintaro Goda (Boys' Tennis), Jack Hotts (Boys' Soccer), Prabhath Inturi (Boys' Tennis), Derrick Kim (Boys' Tennis), Eric Kim (Boys' Tennis), Alex Marine (Boys' Soccer), Neel Nagappala (Boys' Tennis), Rohan Nagaram (Boys' Tennis), Nish Palepu (Boys' Tennis), Vishvaa Ravishankar (Cross Country), Josh Samuelson (Boys' Tennis), Adriano Shauya (Boys' Soccer), and Ava Weeks (Girls' Golf). The students came forward to receive a certificate and congratulations from the Board.

RECOGNITION - ATHENS BOYS' SOCCER STATE CHAMPIONS. The Boys Varsity Soccer team won the MHSAA Division 1 Boys Soccer State Championship on November 4th at Grand Ledge High School. The team finished the year with a record of 20 wins, 3 losses, and 2 ties, and ended the season on a 17-game winning streak. The 2023 State Championship is the 7th boys' soccer state title in school history; Athens has 17 MHSAA state titles. Team members called up for a certificate and congratulations: Emmanuel Aigbedo, Vansh Baxi, Jason Bouna, Charles Ciak, Travis Claypool, Marc Delikat, Luke DiGiovanni, Fares El-Mahrouky, Adam Ethridge, Brody Fahnestock, Gavin Faro, Rodrigo Garcia, Jacob Gruca, Braeden Hupman, John Hupman, Luke Izzo, Daniel Kadiu, Dario Kadiu, Roshan Khan, Griffin LaBay, Ethan Liu, Nik Lulgjuraj, Alex Marine, Joseph Mendrick, Kevin Myrtollari, Miguel Ramirez-Vanegas, Ethan Rem, Brady Roskelly, Nicholas Rossi, and Adriano Shauya.

RECOGNITION - COACHES OF THE YEAR. Athens Boys' Tennis Coach Andrew Shipp was named Coach of the Year by the Michigan High School Tennis Coaches Association. Coach Shipp completed his 18th year leading Athens Varsity Tennis and previously coached Junior Varsity tennis for 5 years. This is the second time he received the award; the first was in 2011. He most recently led the Red Hawks to an 8th place finish at the State Finals in Midland. Athens Boys' Soccer Coach Todd Heugh was named Coach of the Year by the Michigan High School Soccer Coaches Association. Coach Heugh completed his 13th season with Athens Soccer. This is the third time he received the award; the first was in 2002 when he coached at Rochester High School and the second was in 2019 leading Athens. Heugh was also named Great Lakes Regional Coach of the Year by the United Soccer Coaches Association, and most recently led the Red Hawks to an MHSAA Division 1 State Championship.

TSD MISSION MOMENT - SSAB EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE MLK DAY OF SERVICE. The Board recognized the Superintendent Student Advisory Board Executive Committee, whose members lead the 54-member SSAB by planning, setting agendas, running meetings, and orchestrating activities and events. This is the second year an executive board has led the group, made up of eight students. They organized and executed the MLK Citywide Celebration and Day of Service, attended by hundreds of families, with photos shared on the District Facebook page and in the Friday newsletter. Recognized and given a token of the District's appreciation: Marlien William, Aanya Shah, Nurayda Albeez, Kara Crepeau, Elyse Lazrado, Maaz Ali, Niveditha Chandrakanth, and Rachel Asirvatham.

STUDENT SPOTLIGHT. The monthly Student Spotlight recognized creative achievement in the TSD Creative Guild. The Board recognized Jack Kelly, a senior at Athens High School, for his innovative passion in drone technology. Thomas Butcher came forward to describe the work, and a video was shared with the Board showcasing Kelly's talent in driving and controlling a drone.

BOARD RECOGNITION MONTH. Because school closed January 16th for inclement weather, the Board postponed Recognition items to the February meeting to avoid driving on the roads. The District honors its Board of Education trustees each January during School Board Appreciation Month, recognizing board members' role in reinforcing the mission of the Troy School District - ensuring learning for all - and their work in shaping policies, fiscal stewardship, support of world-class teaching and learning, curriculum advancements, infrastructure improvements, and holistic student development. Dr. Machesky thanked the Board for their continued commitment to students and community.

ADDITIONS & DELETIONS: None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS): None. PERSONNEL: None. CURRICULUM: None.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA. Moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt, that BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the Troy Board of Education takes action to approve items A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, and I on the consent agenda: Minutes of the January 9, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; Minutes of the January 16, 2024 Board of Education Organizational & Regular Meeting; Treasurer's Report - December 2023; Schools Closed to Open Enrollment; Schools of Choice 105 & 105c; Course Description Book & New Graduation Requirements; Updated Section 1 Resolution; Districtwide Lawn Mowing 2024-2026; and Cancellation of the March 9, 2024 Board of Education Winter Retreat. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BUSINESS. Deputy Superintendent Rick West stated that the business items had all been discussed thoroughly at the February 6th Board Workshop and that all items are related to Bond work.

Summer 2024 Professional Moving Services. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Philippart that the bid for professional moving services be awarded to Premier Relocations, LLC in the amount of $161,200.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0. Mrs. Anne inquired what happens with the old furniture being replaced; Mr. West indicated they would look for an opportunity to give it to another district in need.

Elementary Playgrounds - Site Work. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Haupt that the bid for playground site work be awarded as follows, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund and the Building Site and Sinking Fund: Concrete, Albanelli Cement Contractors, $394,700.00; Earthwork (Barnard, Bemis and Morse), Dalco Services, LLC, $633,828.00; Earthwork (Hill, Martell, Troy Union), Jacklyn Contracting, $697,000.00; Landscape, Dalco Services, LLC, $344,153.00; Asphalt Paving, Nagle Paving Company, $763,650.00. Bid Total $2,833,331.00; Contingency $283,333.10; TOTAL $3,116,644.10. Yes: 7, No: 0. Mrs. Alic asked to clarify that half of the elementary schools will get the new playgrounds this year and the other half next year, and Mr. West confirmed that is the plan. Mr. Schmidt asked what the earthwork is being done for; Mr. West indicated it is needed to accommodate the new design of playground equipment, for accessibility, and to improve drainage.

Athens HS Stadium Turf & Baker MS Track Replacement Projects. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for Athens Stadium Turf and Baker Track replacement be awarded as follows and approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund and the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0. The award schedule of vendors and amounts does not appear in the minutes text.

Troy HS Athletics Temporary Fencing. Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mr. Hauff that the bid for temporary fencing be awarded to Fencing Connection in the amount of $92,540.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Mrs. Janice Boyer, TEA member and teacher at Bemis Elementary School, addressed the Board about settling the teachers' contract. Mrs. Peggy Chinoski, TSD parent, addressed the Board about recognition of school volunteers and organizations that volunteer and help schools. Mr. Alex Karpowitsch declined to speak but provided Board members with a copy of data on SAT scores. Mr. Gary Koskinen, TSD parent, TEA member and teacher at Athens High School, addressed the Board about working on an expired contract. Mrs. Katie Starn, TEA member and teacher at Leonard Elementary School, addressed the Board about settling the teachers' contract. Mr. Mike DeSantis, TEA member and teacher at Athens High School, addressed the Board about the expiration of the TEA Collective Bargaining Agreement. Mr. Jacob Ritter, senior at Troy High School, addressed the Board regarding the expired teacher contract and classroom learning. Mr. Brian Fahnestock, TEA member and teacher at Baker Middle School, addressed the Board about the expired teacher contract and world class classrooms. Ms. Jamie Hallmark, TEA member and teacher at IA-East, addressed the Board about the expired teacher contract. Mr. Jason Cichowicz, President of the Troy Education Association (TEA), addressed the Board regarding teachers working without a contract and the need to settle the Collective Bargaining Agreement.

OTHER - MASB BOARD OF DIRECTORS' ELECTION, REGION 8. Moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Dr. Wilson that the Troy Board of Education hereby casts its ballot for Birgit McQuiston, Region 8, three-year term, to serve on the 2024 Michigan Association of School Boards' Board of Directors. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS. Dr. Wilson thanked the community for supporting Athens' Charity Week and Troy High's Activist Week and reported attending the MASB Michigan Merit Curriculum Seminar. Mr. Haupt commented on the charity events and how hard the students work for the cause. Mrs. Anne congratulated the Teacher of the Year nominees and winners and reported attending the Advocacy Conference in Washington, DC; she also mentioned the Asian Lunar New Year celebration, Black History Month, and DEI efforts in the District, and congratulated Athens and Troy High on Charity/Activist Week. Mrs. Alic spoke about the school calendar being negotiated as part of the TEA contract and consideration of a diverse calendar, and encouraged everyone to vote on Election Day. Mr. Hauff attended Baker's 7th and 8th grade orchestra concert, noting improvement since the fall performance, and said they will compete on February 29th at Warren Woods High School.

Dr. Machesky announced Preschool Family Night next Wednesday evening; a "Match Day" for CAP (Career Accelerator Program) students, similar to College Signing Day, the following night; Coffee with the Superintendent that Thursday at 7:00 p.m. at Kirby's Coney Island on Crooks Road; and that Monday begins March is Reading Month.

Mr. Schmidt mentioned HB4676 and shared that 40% of foster kids do not graduate from high school, and expressed disappointment with the governor's budget for K-12 education. He announced the next Board Workshop on March 5th at 6:00 p.m. and a Special Meeting at 5:00 p.m. for Closed Session at the Administration Building, with the next Board Meeting on March 19th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building. Schmidt then read a public statement on District and TEA bargaining over the past several months, which has resulted in tentative agreement on 18 specific contractual items. The teams met most recently for a full day of bargaining on Thursday, February 22nd. Previously prohibited topics of bargaining became available due to changes in legislation, and the District team offered language proposals that sparked productive dialogue. The District's team has been waiting two months without response from the TEA to additional contractual language proposals. The District offered three additional bargaining dates, two of which were accepted by the TEA; future scheduled bargaining dates are March 13, March 19, April 3, April 10, and April 16. The District stated it remains committed to a successful agreement providing career advancement for all teachers and positioning the District to attract, retain, and sustain its workforce, with monthly updates provided to the community in this format.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 9:08 p.m.
